title: State of Crypto 2024: Behind the Scenes on Stablecoins, AI, Builder Energy, More
abstract:
PART 1 — ABSTRACT

This conversation critically examines the state of the crypto industry in 2024, drawing on new data about user adoption, infrastructure advances, and evolving applications like stablecoins and decentralized networks. It highlights that after years focused on building basic infrastructure, crypto is entering a phase where improved scalability and lower transaction costs are enabling actual usage growth and more sophisticated applications, although only a small portion of crypto owners are active users. The discussion underscores the persistent challenges in measuring real user activity due to pseudonymity and incentives for bots, the slow but foundational shift in stablecoin payment utility, and the rising entanglement of crypto with broader technological and political trends—including AI adoption and U.S. electoral relevance. Frictions remain on accurately sizing and qualifying user bases, bridging fragmented ecosystems, and translating technical breakthroughs into mainstream, reliable applications; the sector’s future hinges on whether emerging tech can overcome these hurdles to deliver seamless, compelling user experiences.

PART 2 — KEY IDEAS

- There remains significant difficulty and debate in measuring actual human crypto users due to pseudonymous identities and widespread bot activity, especially as airdrop incentives drive large-scale "Sybilling."
- Improved blockchain scalability—mainly through L2s and high-throughput L1s—has dramatically reduced transaction fees, catalyzing higher usage and unlocking new payment and application scenarios.
- The number of monthly transacting crypto users is estimated between 30–60 million, far lower than the number of crypto owners, highlighting an adoption gap and latent growth opportunity.
- Stablecoins have moved from mostly exchange settlement/collateral roles to being viable for everyday payments as lower fees become the norm, enabling new experimentation with consumer payments and international transfers.
- NFT activity has shifted from speculative, high-value trades toward high-volume, low-cost social collecting, made possible by reduced transaction costs; broader, more accessible use cases are emerging.
- Builders’ interest has shifted to inexpensive, scalable blockchains like Solana and Base, but foundational mindshare remains strong on Ethereum and its rollups; infrastructure choices continue to shape the app landscape.
- Crypto’s political visibility has risen: search interest in key swing states is up, possibly influencing U.S. elections, and regulated investment products (like ETPs for Bitcoin/Ethereum) have increased legitimacy and accessibility for traditional investors.
- The intersection with AI is both a narrative and user base trend, suggesting further convergence and mutual influence between these fields, particularly as automated agents become active crypto participants.
- Decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN), social applications, and prediction markets are seeing renewed experimentation, thanks to lower costs and more credible, neutral platforms, though scaling and user experience remain limiting factors.
- Despite infrastructure advances (bridges, L2s), new problems such as fragmentation and interoperability arise, with hopes that forthcoming solutions will shift the industry’s focus from technical plumbing to robust, user-facing applications.
